personas.name: Priya
personas.profile: Frontend lead of six engineers on one React app with a half kept up Storybook, on Chromatic today. She uploads each build from GitHub Actions and accepts or rejects each change on the build page; her goal is that every pull request shows what changed visually and nothing merges until someone has looked.

focus.review: One click from the pull request to the change, few false alarms from anti-aliasing and font hinting, and no red X on every pull request or two clicks to review.
focus.docs: How the commit status and the pull request comment work, so baselines never drift without her knowing why.
focus.cli: An upload step in GitHub Actions that leaves the commit status pending until the changes are approved.

personas.name: Marcus
personas.profile: Platform engineer on a monorepo of about twenty packages (a design system, three apps and the docs) built under a task runner whose cache skips unchanged packages. His goal is one visual check per pull request across every package, without spending CI minutes on packages that did not change.

focus.review: Twenty subprojects with one change each shown as twenty changes in one place, not twenty checks or twenty pages to visit.
focus.docs: A setup that fits the task runner he already has, without each package needing its own configuration.
focus.cli: A skipped package that posts a passed build, so a required check never waits forever for a package the cache skipped.

personas.name: Lena
personas.profile: Design-system maintainer who owns the component library and its tokens, which product teams consume, so one change ripples into every app. Her goal is to catch a token or spacing regression before a consumer ships it, and to know which stories the change touched.

focus.review: A diff measured at the level of a region with a note, twins across themes and viewports, and a way to accept a library-wide change in one step.
focus.docs: How to capture every story in light and dark, from Storybook or from Playwright.
focus.cli: A design-system judge on a local vision model, so a violation is flagged without a screenshot leaving her machine and an intended change does not make noise on every story.

personas.name: Tomás
personas.profile: Engineer at a fintech or health company whose screenshots can show data that looks like customer data, where nothing leaves the network without security sign-off. His goal is visual review with every screenshot kept in-house, self-hosted with Docker or on a box inside the LAN.

focus.review: A self-hosted app with all of the hosted features, and nothing that works only on the hosted app.
focus.docs: A written data flow that lists every outbound call, says plainly where data goes and shows each one off by default.
focus.cli: Local unless told to upload, with no required SaaS call and error reports scrubbed before they leave.

personas.name: Sam
personas.profile: Solo developer or small agency building client sites, often without Storybook, sometimes with Playwright tests and sometimes with only a URL. Sam wants to know in a minute whether a CSS change broke the other pages.

focus.review: A local report.html that opens in a browser and never claims more than it measured.
focus.docs: No sign-up wall and no heavy configuration between Sam and the first answer.
focus.cli: Pair mode against a live URL or two PNG files with no setup and no account, and exit codes that CI can read.
